Let \(h:X\to X\). Then
\[
C_h(S)=h^{-1}(h(S)),
\]
so \(C_h(S)=S\) exactly when \(S\) is a union of fibers of \(h\). Hence
\[
|\{S:C_h(S)=S\}|=2^{|\operatorname{im}h|}.
\]
Also
\[
D_h(S)=\forall_h(h^{-1}S)=(S\cap \operatorname{im}h)\cup (X\setminus \operatorname{im}h),
\]
so \(C_h(S)=D_h(S)=S\) iff \(S=h^{-1}(T)\) for some \(T\subseteq \operatorname{im}h\) and
\[
h(X\setminus \operatorname{im}h)\subseteq T.
\]
Thus the number of such sets is
\[
2^{|\operatorname{im}h|-|h(X\setminus \operatorname{im}h)|}.
\]

Write \(r_k=|\operatorname{im}f^k|\). Since \(|\operatorname{im}f|=2d+2\),
\[
r_1=2d+2.
\]

View \(f\) as a functional digraph. Since \(f\) has no fixed points, every cycle has length at least \(2\). Let \(c\) be the total number of cyclic vertices. Then \(c\ge2\). There are exactly
\[
M-|\operatorname{im}f|=(3d+2)-(2d+2)=d
\]
vertices of indegree \(0\). These are precisely the leaves of the rooted trees feeding into the cycles.

The eventual image size is \(c\), so \(r_k\ge c\ge2\) for all \(k\). Among noncyclic vertices, the number of non-leaves is
\[
(3d+2-c)-d=2d+2-c.
\]
For \(r_2\), a noncyclic vertex survives into \(\operatorname{im}f^2\) only if it has a descendant at distance at least \(2\). Since at most \(d\) noncyclic vertices can have height exactly \(1\), we get
\[
r_2\ge d+2.
\]
Therefore
\[
F(f)=\sum_{k=1}^{M}2^{r_k}
\ge 2^{2d+2}+2^{d+2}+3d\cdot 2^2.
\]
So
\[
A_d=2^{2d+2}+2^{d+2}+12d.
\]

Equality requires \(c=2\), \(r_2=d+2\), and \(r_k=2\) for every \(k\ge3\). Hence the extremal maps are exactly these: a single \(2\)-cycle, and \(d\) disjoint directed chains of length \(3\) feeding into the cycle:
\[
u_i\mapsto v_i\mapsto w_i\mapsto a\ \text{or}\ b,
\]
where \(a\leftrightarrow b\) is the \(2\)-cycle.

Now compute \(G\) for such minimizers.

For \(k=1\), the missing image vertices are the \(u_i\), and their images are the \(v_i\), so
\[
G_1=2^{(2d+2)-d}=2^{d+2}.
\]

For \(k=2\), \(\operatorname{im}f^2\) consists of the \(d\) vertices \(w_i\) and the two cycle vertices. The missing vertices are the \(u_i,v_i\). Their \(f^2\)-images are the \(w_i\) and the cycle vertices hit by the chains. If all chains feed into the same cycle vertex, this image has size \(d+1\), giving
\[
G_2=2^{(d+2)-(d+1)}=2.
\]
If chains feed into both cycle vertices, \(G_2=1\). Thus \(G\) is maximized when all \(d\) chains feed into the same one of the two cycle vertices.

For every \(k\ge3\), the image is just the \(2\)-cycle, and the nonimage vertices map onto both cycle vertices, so
\[
G_k=2^{2-2}=1.
\]
There are \(3d\) such values of \(k\). Hence
\[
B_d=2^{d+2}+2+3d.
\]

Finally count the extremal functions. Choose the two cycle vertices, choose which one receives all chains, then partition the remaining \(3d\) labeled vertices into \(d\) ordered triples \((u_i,v_i,w_i)\):
\[
K_d=\binom{3d+2}{2}\cdot 2\cdot \frac{(3d)!}{d!}
=\frac{(3d+2)!}{d!}.
\]

Therefore
\[
\boxed{(A_d,B_d,K_d)=\left(2^{2d+2}+2^{d+2}+12d,\;2^{d+2}+3d+2,\;\frac{(3d+2)!}{d!}\right)}.
\]
